examples.title: Nocturne: a planetarium's late program, from dusk to the real 22:00 sky (plain CSS)

run.harness: Claude Code 2.1.289, one session resumed for each reply

examples.prompt: /genjutsu:paint build the landing page for Nocturne, the late program of a planetarium in Lisbon.
examples.caption: A new page from an empty React template and a star catalogue. After questions on the mood and the hero, and its two theses shown as a rendered page, the run drew the dome from data/stars.json: 403 stars and Saturn where they stand over Lisbon at 22:00 on 9 October 2026. Scrolling from dusk to night deepens the ground, fades the amber glow at the rim and brings the stars up brightest first. 1440x900 viewport, scaled to 1100x688.

cover.alt: The Nocturne page mid-scroll at dusk: 'The sky on Friday 9 October', with notes on Saturn and the Moon, beside a dome with about half its stars up and the amber glow at its rim half faded; a bar with the times, the prices and Book tickets is pinned at the top.

clip.alt: Scrolling the Nocturne page from dusk to night: the ground deepens from dusk blue to near black, the amber glow at the dome's rim fades, and the stars come up on the dome brightest first; near the end, the star list passes over the dome.

examples.notes: The client accepted both theses at the first showing and asked once for the four problems of the first report to be fixed. The run never saw its page and handed every visual check over. Three defects it introduced are in the receipt: from 1100 px wide the star list runs over the dome (near the end of the clip), a picked star's magnitude line covers its name, and on a phone the hero panel hides the bottom of the dome.

examples.title: Atelier Grès: four firing stages pinned and scrubbed (GSAP ScrollTrigger)
examples.prompt: /genjutsu:cast pin our pottery studio's four firing stages and scrub them with the scroll
examples.caption: The Atelier Grès page, its copy and its four stage blocks are the starting fixture. The run's work is the pinned section, the firing curve it draws, and the stage texts handing over to each other as the scroll scrubs through. 1440x900 viewport, scaled to 1200x750.

cover.alt: The Atelier Grès firing stages section, pinned mid-scrub: the firing curve is drawn up to the glaze firing, and the Glaze firing card shows below it.

clip.alt: Scrolling through the pinned firing stages section of the Atelier Grès page: the firing curve draws from left to right while the Drying, Bisque firing, Glaze firing and Cooling texts take over from each other.

examples.notes: Headless, so the run marked its own thesis UNVALIDATED. It could not build in its sandbox; the build here passed on the first try with no edit.

examples.title: Étale: a slack-water app's beta page, from one real day of NOAA predictions (plain CSS)

run.harness: Claude Code 2.1.289, one session resumed for each reply

examples.prompt: /genjutsu:paint build the landing page for Étale.
examples.caption: A new page from an empty React template and one day of NOAA tide and current predictions. The founder pushed back twice, on an evening alert the read-back underplayed and on a flood the slack card skipped, and the run changed both. Every figure on the page comes from data/tide.json, labelled with its date and station. 1440x900 viewport, scaled to 1200x750: the page loads, holds its first screen, then scrolls to the two charts.

cover.alt: The Étale first screen: the headline 'Slack water off Aquatic Park, before you walk down to the beach.', a slack card showing 05:57 PDT with the current before and after it, and the evening alert drawn as a notification.

clip.alt: The Étale page loading: the headline, the slack card and the alert fade in, the first screen holds, then the page scrolls to the section that sets the slack times against high and low tide in two charts.

examples.notes: A first conversation on the same brief ran just before this one and is not shown. Two defects the run introduced are in the receipt: the dashed slack markers cross the chart labels, and the current line draws once on load, below the fold, so a visitor who scrolls down finds it already drawn.

examples.title: Folio: the "Mark as paid" action (Motion)
examples.prompt: /genjutsu:cast the "Mark as paid" action in our invoice list is dead, make it feel like the money landed
examples.caption: The Folio page is the starting fixture; the motion is the run's work. Two "Mark as paid" clicks: the amount leaves Outstanding and lands in Paid as both totals count, with a signed amount on each card. 1440x900 viewport, cropped; the pointer is drawn in by the recorder, it is not part of the build.

cover.alt: The Folio invoice list 350 ms after a Mark as paid click: Outstanding and Paid are mid-count with a signed amount of 4,200 euros on each card, and the invoice's pill reads Paid.

clip.alt: Two Mark as paid clicks on the Folio invoice list: each time the button slides out, the status pill stamps to Paid, and the Outstanding and Paid totals count by the invoice amount.

examples.notes: Headless, so the run marked its own thesis UNVALIDATED. It introduced one defect its own audit missed: on a shorter window, handing focus to the next unpaid invoice scrolls the page while the totals count (it does not show at 1440x900; the receipt describes when it does).
